events.d: Big new show at the MCA, The Rocks
events.where: Museum of Contemporary Art, The Rocks
events.more: A major exhibition by French artist Philippe Parreno at the Museum of Contemporary Art on Circular Quay.

events.d: Art Gallery of NSW, Naala Badu building
events.where: Art Gallery of NSW, The Domain
events.more: Japanese artist Takashi Murakami's Superflat painting, sculpture and installations, including new work.

events.d: Watch the fleet leave the harbour. Free from the foreshore
events.more: The yacht race to Hobart starts on the harbour at 1pm on Boxing Day. Find a spot on the headlands or harbour foreshore.

events.d: Harbour fireworks. Free vantage points around the foreshore
events.more: One of the biggest fireworks shows in the world. Free vantage points fill up early in the day.

events.d: Weekend markets under the Harbour Bridge

free.d: 6 km clifftop walk past beaches and ocean pools
free.start: Bondi Icebergs, south end of Bondi Beach
free.about: Sydney's most famous walk follows the cliffs from Bondi past Tamarama, Bronte, Clovelly and Gordons Bay to Coogee. It is paved most of the way, with a few steep sets of stairs.
tips: Start at Bondi so the sun is behind you in the morning
Pack swimmers: Bronte and Clovelly are great for a dip
Drinking fountains and toilets at every beach
Bus back to Bondi Junction from Coogee when you finish

free.d: Harbour views from Mrs Macquarie's Chair
free.about: Free gardens right next to the Opera House. Walk around the harbour to Mrs Macquarie's Chair for the classic photo of the Opera House and Harbour Bridge together.
tips: Best photo spot is Mrs Macquarie's Chair at sunrise or sunset
Walk in from Circular Quay along the harbour path
Bring lunch and sit on the lawns

free.d: Sydney's oldest streets, right under the Harbour Bridge
free.about: Cobbled laneways, old pubs and sandstone buildings under the Harbour Bridge. The Rocks Markets run on weekends.
tips: Weekend markets on George Street
Walk up to Observatory Hill for a free bridge view
Some of Sydney's oldest pubs are here

free.d: Free entry to the main collection
free.about: Free general entry to one of Australia's biggest galleries, including the newer Naala Badu building. Some big exhibitions are ticketed.
tips: General admission is free
Check what is on: some exhibitions need a ticket
A short walk from the Botanic Garden

free.d: Cheapest harbour cruise in town, on an Opal card
free.about: The public ferry from Circular Quay to Manly passes the Opera House, the Harbour Bridge and the heads. It costs a normal public transport fare, not a cruise price.
tips: Tap on with an Opal card or your bank card
Sit outside on the right going out for Opera House views
Walk the Manly Corso to the beach when you arrive

events.d: Live at The Northern
Movement, music and talks at Red Devils Park
events.more: A weekend of movement, music and connection. Tickets through the festival website.

events.d: Live at the Beach Hotel
House music at the Beach Hotel
Local makers, food and music at Butler Street Reserve

free.d: Loop to mainland Australia's most easterly point. Whales in season
free.start: The Pass car park (or Captain Cook Lookout)
free.about: The Walgun Cape Byron walking track loops through rainforest, beach, grassland and clifftops up to the lighthouse and the most easterly point of mainland Australia.
tips: Go at sunrise: you will be one of the first in Australia to see it
Whales pass from June to November
Bring water, there are lots of stairs
Parking at the top is paid, so walk from town

free.d: Swim, watch the surfers, catch the sunset
free.about: Main Beach is patrolled and right in town. Walk east along the sand to The Pass to watch the longboarders.
tips: Swim between the flags
Sunset from the sand is free and busy
The Beach Hotel is right behind Main Beach

free.d: Calm bay just below the lighthouse
free.about: A small, sheltered bay under the lighthouse. Good for a calmer swim and spotting dolphins.
tips: Combine it with the lighthouse walk
Dolphins often surf here
Parking is tight, walk in from The Pass

free.d: 1st Sunday, Butler Street Reserve
free.about: Local makers, food and live music on the first Sunday of the month.
tips: Get there early before it gets hot
Bring cash for some stalls

events.d: International cricket on the Gold Coast
Free movie on the sand by the Surfers Paradise sign, fireworks at 8pm
events.more: Bring a towel: family movies on the sand from 7pm and fireworks at 8pm each Sunday before Christmas.

events.d: 80s and 90s classics at Retro's, Orchid Ave
Night markets on the Esplanade

free.d: Patrolled surf beach right in town
free.start: The Esplanade, end of Cavill Avenue
free.about: The famous Gold Coast beach, patrolled year round, at the end of Cavill Avenue.
tips: Swim between the flags
Night markets on the Esplanade on Wednesday, Friday and Sunday

free.d: Street life, buskers and the night strip
free.about: The heart of Surfers: shops, buskers, bars and the beachfront Esplanade.
tips: Busiest from about 8pm
Orchid Avenue has most of the clubs

free.d: Grassy beachfront park for a lazy afternoon
free.about: Big grassy park on the beach at Broadbeach, with barbecues and shade.
tips: Free barbecues
A short tram ride south of Surfers

free.d: Rainforest headland walk with surf views
free.about: The Oceanview walk goes around the rocky headland from Burleigh to Tallebudgera Creek. Come back over the top on the Rainforest circuit for views up to Surfers.
tips: Watch the surfers at The Point first
Whales in winter and spring
Stay on the track: the boulder fields are off limits

events.when: Most nights in Dec (2026 dates TBC)
events.d: Free Christmas light show on City Hall, King George Square
events.more: A free light and sound show projected onto City Hall. Runs every 15 minutes in the evenings in the lead-up to Christmas.

events.when: Mid to late Dec (2026 dates TBC)
events.d: Christmas markets, carols and open-air cinema
Shipping-container street food markets

free.d: Free man-made beach and lagoon in the city
free.about: A patrolled lagoon with a sandy beach in the middle of the city, across the river from the CBD.
tips: Lifeguards on duty
Free barbecues in the parklands nearby

free.d: Free ferry along the Brisbane River
free.time: About an hour end to end
free.about: The free red CityHopper ferry runs up and down the river, stopping at South Bank, the CBD and Kangaroo Point.
tips: Free, no card needed
Great at sunset

free.d: City skyline views, best at sunset
free.about: Old cliffs right on the river with the best view of the city skyline. Climbers and abseilers use them during the day.
tips: Come for sunset and stay as the city lights up
Stairs lead down to the riverside path

free.d: Free, inside City Hall
free.start: Level 3, City Hall, King George Square
free.about: Free museum about the city, inside the old City Hall.
tips: Entry is free
City Hall clock tower tours are popular, check times

free.d: Big gardens on the edge of the CBD
free.about: One of the world's largest subtropical gardens in a city centre, next to Roma Street station.
tips: Right next to the train and bus station
Good shaded walk on a hot day

events.d: Free live music in the gardens
Santa's beach hut and sunset carols on Main Beach
Big markets in the hinterland, a short bus ride away

free.d: Headland track to Hell's Gates. Koalas in the trees
free.dist: 2.7 km one way to Hell's Gates
free.grade: Easy to Dolphin Point, then some steps
free.start: Noosa National Park day-use area, Park Road
free.about: Follows the headland past Boiling Pot and Dolphin Point to Hell's Gates. The path is sealed to Dolphin Point, then unsealed with some steps and steep sections.
tips: Look up: koalas sit in the gum trees by the track
Watch for turtles and dolphins at Dolphin Point
Beaches in the park are not patrolled, so swim at Main Beach
Walk in from Hastings Street along the boardwalk

free.d: Calm, patrolled and right off Hastings Street
free.about: North-facing and sheltered, so it is usually calm. Patrolled all year.
tips: Good for learning to surf
Sunset from the beach is popular

free.d: Wide surf beach a short bus ride away
free.about: Bigger surf and fewer people than Main Beach. You can also walk here through the national park.
tips: Catch the local bus from Noosa Junction
Swim between the flags

free.d: Sunset walk along Gympie Terrace
free.about: A flat riverside path with views across the water. Busy at sunset.
tips: Bring takeaway and eat on the grass
Flat, easy walking

events.d: Carols, sausage sizzle and Santa at the Community Centre

free.d: Giant sand dune with views over Rainbow Beach
free.dist: 600 m one way from the car park
free.time: About an hour with time on the dune
free.start: Carlo Sandblow car park, top of Cooloola Drive
free.about: A 15-hectare 'moonscape' of sand on the cliffs above Rainbow Beach, with views to Double Island Point and K'gari.
tips: Best at sunrise or sunset when the sand is cool
From town it is about 1.5 km uphill, or start at the car park
Do not try to get down to the beach from the dune

free.d: Walk the beach under the cliffs at low tide
free.about: Walk south along the sand to the cliffs that gave Rainbow Beach its name, with dozens of shades of red, orange and yellow sand.
tips: Go at low tide only
Watch for 4WDs on the beach
Bring water and a hat, there is no shade

free.d: Patrolled surf beach right in town
free.about: The main beach in town, patrolled by lifesavers.
tips: Swim between the flags
4WDs use the beach, so keep an eye out

free.d: Watch the barges head to K'gari
free.about: The point where the barges leave for K'gari. A great spot for sunset over the water.
tips: About 15 minutes by car from town
Bring insect repellent at dusk

events.d: Weekly yacht racing at the Whitsunday Sailing Club. Novices can join a crew
Carols and a movie on the foreshore
Free fireworks over the water
On the foreshore by the lagoon

free.d: Free swimming lagoon right on the foreshore
free.about: A big free lagoon with lawns and shade, in the middle of town. Safe from stingers and crocodiles.
tips: Free and open every day
Markets run next to it on Saturday mornings

free.d: Waterfront path from town to Cannonvale
free.about: A boardwalk and path along the water from the lagoon past the marina and Shingley Beach to Cannonvale Beach. The full length reopened after upgrades in mid 2026.
tips: Go early morning or late afternoon, it is hot in the middle of the day
Look out for turtles from the boardwalk
Cafes along the way

free.d: Saturday morning markets on the foreshore
free.about: Local food, crafts and souvenirs by the lagoon every Saturday morning.
tips: On from about 7am to 1pm
Go early before it gets hot

free.d: Wednesdays at the Sailing Club. Ask to join a crew
free.about: Weekly twilight yacht racing at the Whitsunday Sailing Club. Novices can ask to join a crew.
tips: Turn up early and ask at the club
Results and drinks at the club afterwards

events.d: Horseshoe Bay foreshore. Closed Feb and Mar

free.d: Old WWII forts and wild koalas on the way up
free.about: Magnetic Island's most popular walk climbs to World War II gun emplacements and a lookout over the bays. Wild koalas often sit in the trees beside the track.
tips: Go early morning for koalas and cooler air
Bring water, there is little shade at the top
Watch koalas quietly from a distance

free.d: Long beach with cafes and sunset drinks
free.about: The island's longest beach, with cafes and bars along the front.
tips: Stinger net in season
Sunday markets on the foreshore

free.d: Sheltered bay for a swim and a snorkel
free.about: A small, sheltered bay between granite boulders. Good snorkelling off the rocks.
tips: Patrolled in season
Bring a snorkel

free.d: Sundays at Horseshoe Bay
free.about: Jewellery, clothes, art and food every Sunday. Closed in February and March.
tips: Pair it with breakfast at the bay

events.d: Under the trees at Ulysses Park on Porter Promenade

free.d: 14 km of beach between rainforest and reef
free.about: A long, quiet beach backed by rainforest, looking out to Dunk Island.
tips: Swim in the stinger net in season
Croc warning signs apply near creeks

free.d: Coastal walk with turtle and island views
free.start: South Mission Beach boat ramp, Kennedy Esplanade
free.about: Starts with a boardwalk to Lovers Beach, then follows the rocky shore and small beaches round to Kennedy Bay. Lookouts are good for spotting turtles.
tips: Check the tide: some sections are on the beach
Look for turtles from the lookouts
Bring water and a hat

free.d: Rainforest climb with views to Dunk Island. Watch for cassowaries
free.about: A loop up through rainforest in Clump Mountain National Park to a lookout over the coast and Dunk Island. One of the best places to see a wild cassowary.
tips: Go early morning for cassowaries
Keep your distance from cassowaries and never feed them
Limited shade, so carry water

free.d: 1st & 3rd Sunday at Ulysses Park
free.about: Local markets under the trees by the beach on the first and third Sunday of the month.
tips: Bring cash for smaller stalls

events.when: From Sun 29 Nov, Fri to Sun nights to 24 Dec
events.d: Free lights along the Esplanade, 6 to 9pm
events.more: Christmas Light Lane starts at Lagoon Plaza and winds along the waterfront to the Eastern Event Lawn.

events.d: Over 130 stalls on Williams Esplanade
Free carols at Munro Martin Parklands
Free concert, fireworks at 8:30pm and midnight
Food court, massages and souvenirs

free.d: Free saltwater swimming lagoon on the waterfront
free.about: Cairns has no swimming beach in town, so this free lagoon is where everyone cools off. It's patrolled and safe from stingers and crocodiles.
tips: Free and open every day
Free barbecues along the Esplanade

free.d: Sunset walk past the mudflats and pelicans
free.about: A flat waterfront boardwalk north from the lagoon, past mudflats full of birds. Lovely at sunset.
tips: Bring insect repellent at dusk
Do not go near the water: crocodiles live here

free.d: Food and stalls every night in the city
free.about: Food court, massages and souvenir stalls, open every night.
tips: Cheap dinner option
Right next to the Esplanade

free.d: Free gardens and boardwalks in Edge Hill
free.about: Free tropical gardens with rainforest boardwalks, a short bus ride from the city.
tips: Free entry
Bring insect repellent
